text:
maria: heads up — us-west1 gpu pending is up ~18% over the last hour. small training jobs (tiny-gang) stuck in PENDING, eviction spikes on older racks :frowning:

 tj: saw that. any network errors in the attach logs? or is this pure scheduling NoFit?

 maria: quick grep of scheduler events shows a lot of "NoNodesAvailable" with reasons: Insufficient GPUs and NodeAffinity mismatches. also some "AttachVolume timeout" for gpu-node PVCs. paste of scheduler snippet:

 ```text
 I0301 14:22:11.123 scheduler_pred: Pod default/model-train-12 NoNodesAvailable: 0/120 nodes are available: 80 Insufficient gpu.com/gpu, 40 node(s) had taint {gpu-exclusive: true}
 ``` 

 linh: hmm we recently rolled the rack-label selector that prefers `gpu-v2` family in the scheduler plugin. maybe older `gpu-v1` nodes got deprioritized, causing backfill to fail. @ops-bot can you dump node counts per label?

 ops-bot: node-counts for us-west1 as of now: `gpu-v2: 32`, `gpu-v1: 48`, `gpu-preemptible: 16` ; available GPUs= (v2:96, v1:192, preemptible:16)

 tj: wait v2 is fewer but preferred — that mismatch could cause binpack to try place on v2 and fail then not fallback quickly. can we check scheduler policy? maybe the topologySpread or priority plugin got stricter.

 andre: also noticed egress throttling in us-west1 earlier which inflated attach latency for NVMe versus nfs PVs. that delay can time out attach and trigger evictions. brief klog from kubelet:

 ```text
 W0301 14:23:02.987 kubelet_attach: attach timeout for volume gpu-nvme-123 after 30s, retrying
 ``` 

 maria: so two parallel problems: flavor-preference + attach latency. short-term mitigation options?

 linh: 1) relax family preference in the scheduler profile (canary to 5% of schedulers), 2) add a temporary tolerant-taint rule to allow v1 nodes for tiny-gang pods, 3) bump NVMe attach timeout and retry logic in kubelet agent.

 tj: option 2 seems fastest. we can add `tolerations` via mutating webhook for jobs tagged `tiny-gang=true`. low blast radius and immediate effect.

 maria: agree. deploy patch to webhook canary around 14:50.

 ops-bot: canary rollout scheduled: webhook-mutator v1.2 -> 5% of admission controllers at 14:50 UTC. will watch for evictions metric.

 andre: cost note — v1 nodes are cheaper per GPU but force more inter-rack traffic for some workloads. relaxing affinity will likely increase cross-az egress on some jobs. estimate: +8% egress cost on affected jobs.

 maria: fine for now, prefer stability. long-term: we should update our `flavor-fallback` policy: fast fallback to compatible families when preferred family cannot satisfy binpack within 5s. file a follow-up? @linh

 linh: filing PERF-ops ticket after this thread. :thumbsup:

 tj: i'll watch PENDING count, if it drops under 3% in 20m we roll to 50%.

 maria: thanks. postmortem if rollout needed. :eyes:
